title: EDM-TECH-130BPM
author: Various
description:
Over 1000 techno loops at the specified BPM, featuring drum machine and percussive drum synths, complemented by additional synthesizers and chords. Each BPM set is different!
EDM-TECH is an open-source corpus of drum recordings produced in the techno genre, consisting of 11,270 WAV files paired with JSON metadata for supervised model training. The dataset was generated using custom scripting applied to a proprietary database of MIDI patterns and one-shot drum samples. Recordings primarily feature drum machine and percussive drum synths, complemented by additional samples of synthesizers and chords. Data augmentation included random sample-swapping, track isolation, pitch-shifting, equalization, and convolution reverb modeling. These strategies enhance model generalization by exposing training examples to diverse rhythms, sonic qualities, and ambient effects. Training examples were randomly mixed with varying signal levels and audio qualities, providing examples that reflect the evolving styles of techno music over the decades.
WaivOps is a crowd-sourced music creator project focused on providing newly sourced music datasets for developing generative AI models. Unlike commonly sourced audio and MIDI training data, these datasets are specifically developed to enhance model performance by augmenting and generalizing musical notations. Each dataset is developed with model objectives in mind, offering developers and AI music enthusiasts access to large-scale data for various tasks involved in pretraining and fine-tuning models.
The datasets are licensed under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). For more detailed information, please visit the links provided to GitHub or Zenodo.

title: Salamander Drumkit
author: Alexander Holm
description:
A drum sample library I recorded in the garage! It’s meant to have an acoustic sound/feel to it. It turned out pretty well. It doesn't have many velocity layers, but instead many samples per velocity, in an attempt to get a more authentic sound when programming. The closed-hat has no less than 20 samples per velocity... only two velocity layers tho, so that makes 40 in total. I've actually built the drumkit myself (in 2009). It's built out of birch staves and has very thick shells (couldn't lathe the insides) It also features an unusual one of a kind ropetuning system, the 12" tomtom is a prototype of another kind tho tuning system. Drums:
+ 12x7" racktom, Aquarian modern vintage (not the one in the picture...)
+ 14x14" floortom, Remo emperor or evans g2 can't remember for shure.
+ 18x18" kick, Remo pinstripe, Coated Ambassador on the resonant side.
+ 14x5" snare birchstaves with thin mahogany stripes, Evans power center reverse dot, Coated.
+ 14x6" snare2 birch and mahogany staves, Evans genera dry Coated, with most of the muffling ring ripped off.
Cymbals:
+ Paiste 18" Innovations china (china2)
+ Paiste 18" Innovations medium crash (crash1)
+ Paiste 20" Rude thin crash (crash2)
+ Paiste 20" pst5 medium ride (ride1)
+ Paiste 8" pst5 splash
+ Paiste 6" accent
+ Stagg 20" SH medium ride (ride 1)
+ Stagg 14" SH hihat
+ Stagg 16" SH crash (crash3)
+ Masterworks 20" Custom china (china1)

title: Virtual Playing Orchestra (VPO3)
author: various
description:
Virtual Playing Orchestra v3 is a free orchestral sample library, in sfz format, that was created to emulate multiple articulations of the solo and section instruments from a full orchestra using the best free samples from Sonatina Symphonic Orchestra, No Budget Orchestra, VSCO2 Community Edition, University of Iowa, Philharmonia Orchestra and extra free samples from Mattias Westlund, author of Sonatina Symphonic Orchestra. It offers an extensive selection of section and solo instruments for woodwinds, brass, strings, and percussion.
The package contains 2 sets of instruments:
+ The Standard Orchestra uses key velocity (how fast you hit a key on your MIDI controller) to control the volume. Articulations (sustain, staccato etc) are placed in different tracks or are selected via key switches. Most virtual instruments work this way.
+ The Performance Orchestra uses the MOD wheel to control volume (some professional sample libraries work this way). Key velocity (how fast you hit a key on your MIDI controller) selects the articulation (sustain, staccato etc) while still slightly affecting the volume. The performance .sfz file names contain the string '-PERF'.

author: Various
description:
A collection of hydriogen2 drumkits that you can use in zynthian with Fabla and DrMr sampler. Most of included kits are drum-machines from 80s & 90s, but it also includes the ethnic percussion kit 'CircAfrique v4' and others.
Note that many of the original kits don't mute their open hi-hat sounds when the hi-hat closed sound is triggered. The hi-hat group settings have been adjusted for most of this collection to mute the open hat when the closed hat is triggered.

title: jRhodes3d - Stereo Rhodes MK I
author: Jeff Learman
description:
jRhodes3 is my sampling of my 1977 Rhodes Mark I Stage 73 electric piano, which I purchased new back in 1978. This sample set is not intended to be a jack-of-all-trades Rhodes, but rather, it's how I usually set up and used my Rhodes. It was recorded with EQ, with a treble boost and low-mid scoop, emphasizing the bell tones, and with substantial bark on the higher velocity layers. There are 5 layers, sampled to peak at 3dB difference per layer at on the low notes and to maintain volume throughout each layer. Not all layers are full-keyboard width, as higher notes don't change timbre as much. The set includes 67 x 16-bit full-length samples, with up to 5 velocity layers, sampling every 4th white key. The samples were recorded directly from the harp connector. Samples are encoded in lossless FLAC format to reduce disk space. Two versions are provided, each with and without velocity cross-fading: - Mono
- Stereo - a mild stereo chorus
Effects:
Stereo-width, tremolo and auto-pan are implemented using SFZ opcodes. Since stereo effect are applied using mid-side technique, the effect cancels out completely in mono. However, stereo versions use two voices per note, so use mono version to get more polyphony. Controllers:
- CC7: Main Volume
- CC10: Pan
- CC76: Stereo Width (0 - 200%)
- CC1 (Mod wheel): Tremolo Amplitude (0 - 6 dB)
- CC92: Tremolo Frequency (0.1 - 10 Hz)
- CC94: AutoPan Depth (0 - 100%)
- CC95: AutoPan Frequency (0.1 - 10 Hz)
- CC97: FX delay - Start Time (0 - 2 secs)
- CC98: FX delay - Fade-in Time (0 - 2 secs)
Keyswitches:
Use keyswitches to select version and with or without velocity crossfades. Velocity crossfades smooth the transitions between velocity layers, but with two negative side effects. The number of voices used per note is doubled, and on the Rhodes, low notes get some phasing, because the Rhodes low notes go a bit sharp when struck harder. - G7: Stereo with velocity crossfade (default)
- Ab7: Stereo without velocity crossfade
- A7: Mono with velocity crossfade
- Bb7: Mono without velocity crossfade
(*) C4 is Middle C (ISO Scientific Pitch Notation)

title: TR808 Fischer
author: Michael Fischer (samples) & Jeff Learman (SFZ)
description: Sample-based Roland TR-808 drum machine emulation with all the sound controllers from the original device plus individual pan control for each sound. It uses the Fischer's sampleset, composed of 116 high quality samples recorded directly from the original device at different control positions. TR808.sfz The original sound without blend. Only 5 control positions for the controllers, but you get the purest TR808 sound. TR808_xfades.sfz It blends 2 samples to simulate intermediate controller values. Not the purest sound, but increased control possibilities.

title: VS Chamber Orchestra (VSCO2)
author: Versilian Studios LLC.
description:
VSCO 2 Community Edition (CE) is an open-source, open-ended subset of the main VSCO 2 library designed for young composers, hobbyist sample library developers, and students around the world to create better sounding music for free and learn more about the process of sample library development.
The samples are mapped with no significant tweaks or changes to the sounds or their layout. As a result, the sound is natural and great for ambient and calm orchestral, but may seem a little 'loose' if you are used to General MIDI soundfonts or synthesizers.
The samples have been recorded by Sam Gossner & Simon Dalzell. Sample Cutting by Elan Hickler/Soundemote.

title: VCSL Keys
author: Versilian Studios LLC.
description: This collection contains all of the keyboard instruments from the Versilian Community Sample Library (VCSL) in one convenient package. It contains 3 grand pianos, 2 upright pianos, and 5 harpsichords, all derived from Versilian Studios commercial libraries. SFZ patches have been created by Peter Eastman. Natural Pianos Five sampling sessions of four different pianos are included here as well, models “K”, “S”, “Y”, and “Knight”. All of these instruments are vintage or antique, most have had rough lives in practice rooms and rehearsal halls. What you hear is the real sound of pianos “in the wild”, not some artificially perfected studio tone or modelled sound. These are not archival instruments kept in dust-proof rooms and tuned between every note, but rather working, living pianos with quirks and imperfections. Pianos “S” and “Knight” both feature sustain pedal samples, and all pianos feature releases. Harpsichords The harpsichord is a unique historical keyed instrument which uses small plectra to pluck the strings, unlike a piano which uses a hammer to strike the keys. Over the years, Versilian Studios has sampled many harpsichords, but few have made it to commercial release. Exclusive to this set is the English Harpsichord, a kit harpsichord from the 1970’s, which sounds truly amazing in pop and classic rock contexts! For most instruments, separate Release samples are included for realism.

title: Zynthian Meatbass
author: Karoryfer Lecolds
description:
Karoryfer Meatbass for Zynthian This an upright bass plucked (pizzicato), intended to be suitable for jazz/blues/bluegrass on Zynthian. It is a reduced version of Karoryfer Meatbass, which is freely available at Karoryfer. This version was reduced from the original by Jeff Learman. Notes above SPN C5 (an octave above Middle C) are common percussive noises made on the bass, such as slaps. Controls
  • cc7 - Master Vol
  • cc10 - Master Pan
  • cc100 - Attack
  • cc101 - Hold
  • cc102 - Decay
  • cc103 - Sustain
  • cc104 - Release
  • cc111 - Vibrato Depth
  • cc112 - Vibrato Speed
  • cc115 - Vibrato Delay
  • cc116 - Vibrato Fadev
  • cc117 - Humanize Rate
  • cc118 - Uneven Pitch
  • cc119 - Unsteady Vibrato
From original README for Karoryfer Meatbass Meatbass is a sample library for Plogue Sforzando version 1.845 or newer. It contains samples of a 1958 Otto Rubner double bass played and mapped by Drogomir Smolken, recorded by Ludwik Zamenhof. Fifths tuning (CGDA), Thomastik-Infeld Spirocore strings. F.G. Pfretzschner bow, Pops' rosin. Plucked notes with four velocity layers and four round robins, and percussive noises with round robins, above the notes

title: Accurate Salamander Grand Piano
author: Chisato Yamauchi; Samples from Alexander Holm
description:
The Accurate Salamander Project has remastered existing sample sets to produce new Grand Piano soundbanks (SFZ) of instrument maker-level quality. It uses a physics-based approach,  thoroughly pursuing the 'homogeneity' and 'continuity' of volume, overtone, envelope, and delay, which are directly related to ease of control and important for performers who handle delicate expressions.
The Salamander Grand Piano (the widely used SFZ soundbank) with its high recording quality was used as the original source set, and all 480 sampled data in it were carefully re-mastered. We spend a great deal of time setting up and adjusting the processing system in order to achieve perfect quality (at the limit level of specifications). In addition to minimal filtering to preserve the original tone, spot noise that may have been caused by the recording was removed, vibratory noise from sources other than the hammers and strings was eliminated, and extensive restoration was performed to adjust the tone caused by the condition of the piano used for sampling (deteriorated hammers, lack of tuning, etc.) and to correct fatal problems.

title: Zynthian Factory SF2s
author: Various
description: A collection of SF2 soundfonts from different sources, categorized by instrument type. This collection part of the 'factory' collection and it's required by some demo snapshots.

title: Osiris Piano for Zynthian
author: Sam Gossner, DSmolken
description: A soft warm grand piano. A unique quiet piano based in a worn Yamaha C2 grand recorded at half- stick with the soft pedal down and very low dynamics. This version removes several features of the original Osiris piano to achieve a smaller footprint, best suited for zynthian usage.

title: MelloSFZotron
author: Nathan Ingelbrecht
description:
Mellotron SFZ based on the lovely Leisureland samples. This is an effort to make a software equivalent of a Mellotron. All the controls like on a real Mellotron are available. You get a tune knob that can go +1 octave and -1 octave. There's also a tone knob which you will need because fully clockwise the sounds are pretty harsh. I've also added an attack and release knob which where not on the Mellotron but are a nice extra.
As a final touch there is aftertouch response. When used it adds +6dB gain and slows the pitch down by 30 cents. After reading about Mellotrons on the web it appeared that the M400 sometimes had a felt strip underneath the keys, which enabled the player to press the tape-head a little harder against the tape. I assume this made the sounds louder but also slowed down the tape a little bit because of drag. This is the effect I tried to recreate. If someone has a real Mellotron, feel free to comment.

title: Sonatina Symphonic Orchestra (SSO4)
author: Mattias Westlund, Peter Eastman
description:
Sonatina Symphonic Orchestra (SSO) is a free library of sampled orchestral instruments. The original version was created by Mattias Westlund in 2011, and quickly earned a following for its excellent quality and wide selection of instruments.
All samples are stereo, 16 bit, 44.1 kHz. Most instruments are sampled in minor 3rds. Most short articulations use at least 2x round robin.
Most samples have only a small amount of reverb baked into them, so adding a realistic reverb is important for producing a good overall sound. Given that the samples came from a variety of different sources, this is also important for making them sound like a unified orchestra.

title: Accurate Salamander Grand for Zynthian
author: Chisato Yamauchi; Samples from Alexander Holm
description:
Accurate Salamander Grand tailored for Zynthian.
The Accurate Salamander Project has remastered existing sample sets to produce new Grand Piano soundbanks (SFZ) of instrument maker-level quality. It uses a physics-based approach,  thoroughly pursuing the 'homogeneity' and 'continuity' of volume, overtone, envelope, and delay, which are directly related to ease of control and important for performers who handle delicate expressions.
The Salamander Grand Piano (the widely used SFZ soundbank) with its high recording quality was used as the original source set, and all 480 sampled data in it were carefully re-mastered. We spend a great deal of time setting up and adjusting the processing system in order to achieve perfect quality (at the limit level of specifications). In addition to minimal filtering to preserve the original tone, spot noise that may have been caused by the recording was removed, vibratory noise from sources other than the hammers and strings was eliminated, and extensive restoration was performed to adjust the tone caused by the condition of the piano used for sampling (deteriorated hammers, lack of tuning, etc.) and to correct fatal problems.
This version was tailored for Zynthian by converting (normalized) samples to 16 bits and using FLAC lossless compression.  Hammer noise, release samples, and resonance samples are all retained. Half-pedaling is enabled, and release time is set to a curve simulating a grand piano.

title: Zynthian Factory SFZs from Github (NEW)
author: Various
license: Various (GPL, MIT, CC0, CC-BY-SA, and unknown)
description:
This collection is an update of the 'factory' collection and is compatible with it, except that Guitars/RealBanjo has been removed. NOTE: the original factory SFZ package must be removed first.
Likewise, this package must be removed before re-installing the original factory SFZ package.

title: Linnoleum SFZ
author: Nathan Ingelbrecht
description:
Linn LM-1 SFZ based on samples provided by the nice people at Samples From Mars, made available for their article involving the comparison of 2 LM-1 revisions. One is black and one is grey. I tried to make a software equivalent of the LM-1 with the available samples. This means the controls are limited to volume, pan, tune and decay. This does not mean a limitation on the quantity of knobs to twist.
Quote from the article: 'The orange LM1 (Rev.3) has a harder, punchier and faster sound (almost like a 707), while the mysterious, gray unit (Rev.2) is warmer and lazier. Something about the bass drum filters sound completely different between the two, and the cabasa is either a different sample entirely, has more distortion, pre-attack, or all of the above. The orange unit also has a modded snare sample with less pre-attack, so that it arrives a bit earlier when sequenced. All of these differences give each machine their own distinct sound, feel and pocket.'

title: Soul Band Brass Section
author: Jeff Learman (sfz only)
description:
Soul Band Brass Section for live keyboard use. REQUIRES VSCO2! Each note plays up to four instruments: - trombone
- tenor sax
- alto sax
- trumpet
Each instrument has volume and octave shift CC control. By default, all instruments play at the same volume, with no octave shift. NOTE! This sfz uses samples from other packages. REQUIRED PACKAGES: - Zynthian Factory SFZ's
- VSCO2
Image by Shein from Jersey City, USA - Earth, Wind, and Fire, CC BY 2.0, https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=5194719

title: jSteelDrum
author: Jeff Learman
description:
C Steel Pan (Steel Drum) - Hand-made oil-drum steel drum.
- 24 notes sampled, C4 (middle C) to B5
- 5 velocity layers, with or without velocity crossfades
- 3 or 4 samples per zone (that is, per note per layer)
- Stereo 16 bit, 44.1 KHz samples
- Unlooped
- 44 MB, FLAC format
There are two versions of the .sfz file, one with velocity crossfades and one without. The velocity crossfades work extremely well, and since we play only a few notes at a time on steel drum, the extra voice requirement is reasonable, even on Zynthian. About the instrument This is a sampling of a steel drum (a.k.a. 'steel pan') hand-made in Trinidad and sold by Hopetown Music of Long Beach CA, around 2005. (See photo & PDF.) The samples were recorded in September 2021. Samples were recorded in mid-side stereo using an AT4033a as the mid mic and a Studio Projects B3 as the side mic. Controls Use the Mod wheel (CC1) to control stereo depth. With the mod wheel in the center (50%), the stereo depth is 100% (normal.) Pull the wheel all the way down to get pure mono, or push above 50% to get an extra wide image, or anything in between. When you load the sampleset, the depth will be 100% even if the mod wheel is not at zero, but if you move the mod wheel, the depth will change accordingly.

title: X42 IRs
author: Various
description: A collection of Impulse Response (IRs) files and the corresponding LV2 presets for the excellent X42's IR convolver plugin. Sourced from ccgb, jezwells, l480, openairlib, samplicity-m7 and teufelsberg.

title: Teatre Fortuny
author: Zylvio & Jofemodo
description:
A collection of IRs captured and processed with zynthian in the 'Teatre Fortuny' at Reus (Spain). Not a really serious work with surprisingly good results. We recorded in three positions along the central corridor of the theatre, four different recordings for each position: + A sine sweep played through the theatre’s PA, recorded in stereo with small condenser mics.
+ The same sweep recorded in mono with an AKG 414 XLS in omni position.
+ A hand-clap recorded in stereo with small condenser mics.
+ A hand-clap recorded in mono with an AKG 414 XLS in omni position.
Yes, the PA was used as the emitter. Yes, it colors the sound. No, we weren’t trying to be purists. This was more about exploration (and fun) than laboratory conditions. The entire session was recorded through a humble Scarlett 2i2. The post-processing (deconvolution) of the sine-sweep recordings was made with zynthian. The clap recordings were trimmed and adjusted in a PC with Audacity.

title: Conner's IR Library
author: Conners
description: A collection of impulse response files that you can load with the X42's IR convolver plugins and others. It's a huge collection of well organized, mostly experimental IRs. It will surprise you.
